parts: Equations of a line in space

Through a point a parallel to b: r = a + λb. Cartesian: (x − x₁)/a = (y − y₁)/b = (z − z₁)/c, where a, b, c are direction ratios. Through two points: r = a + λ(b − a), i.e. (x − x₁)/(x₂ − x₁) = (y − y₁)/(y₂ − y₁) = (z − z₁)/(z₂ − z₁).
A term like z = −1 in (x − 2)/3 = (y − 5)/(−2), z = −1 means the direction ratio in z is 0.
Any point on a line: (x₁ + aλ, y₁ + bλ, z₁ + cλ) — use it to find points at a given distance.
cos θ = |a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ + c₁c₂|/(√(a₁² + b₁² + c₁²)√(a₂² + b₂² + c₂²)). A line given as the intersection of two planes has direction n₁ × n₂.
Lines through A (direction d₁) and B (direction d₂) are coplanar when (B − A)·(d₁ × d₂) = 0. The plane containing them has normal d₁ × d₂ and passes through A.
